# `silk/schema/report`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Show the problems a schema found, as source snippets, one line each, or JSON.

## When to use
Call [`SchemaReport.write`](#SchemaReport.impl.write) with the `silk.schema.issue.SchemaErrors` from
`silk.schema.json.SchemaJson.decodeAll`, or [`SchemaReport.writeOne`](#SchemaReport.impl.writeOne) with the one
`SchemaError` from `SchemaJson.decode`, and the input they were read from. Pick
[`ReportOptions.snippet`](#ReportOptions.impl.snippet) for a terminal, [`ReportOptions.line`](#ReportOptions.impl.line) for logs and editors' problem
matchers, and [`ReportOptions.json`](#ReportOptions.impl.json) for tools and for sending the problems back to a model.

## Details
A report cuts the found value out of the input by its span, at most 40 bytes of it, and counts
lines and columns only while it writes: lines and columns start at 1, and columns count
characters, as editors do. [`ReportOptions.redacted`](#ReportOptions.impl.redacted) writes only the kind of each found value,
such as `got text`, for input that may hold secrets. A snippet shows at most about 80 characters
of a long line, around the problem.

The snippet form looks like this:

```text
 --> server.json:3:11 at port
  |
3 |   "port": 0,
  |           ^ expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0
```

The line form writes `server.json:3:11: port: expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0`, and
the JSON form writes one object, `{"problems": [...], "dropped": 0}`, whose paths are JSON
Pointers into the input.

## Examples
### Write every problem of a config
```silk
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaErrors }
import silk.schema.json { SchemaJson }
import silk.schema.report { ReportOptions, SchemaReport }
import silk.schema.schema { Schema, Spec }

struct Server {
  pub port: u16,
  pub workers: u8,
}

impl Schema for Server {
  static fn spec() -> Spec<Server> {
    return Spec<Server>.of() |> Spec<Server>.between("port", 1, 65535)
  }
}

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 512],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    let mut at: usize = 0
    while at < val.length {
      if self.length < 512 { self.bytes[self.length] = val[at] }
      self.length = self.length + 1
      at = at + 1
    }
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn check() -> usize ! OutOfMemoryError | WriterError ? &mut Allocator {
  let input = b"{\"port\": 0, \"workers\": 300}"
  let mut capture = Capture {bytes: [0; 512], length: 0}
  match move run Effect.result(SchemaJson.decodeAll<Server>(input)) {
    Result<Server, SchemaErrors | OutOfMemoryError>.Failure {error} => match move error {
      SchemaErrors problems => {
        run SchemaReport.write(&problems, input, "server.json", ReportOptions.line()) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
      }
      OutOfMemoryError {} => { fail OutOfMemoryError {} }
    }
    _ => {}
  }
  // server.json:1:10: port: expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0
  // server.json:1:24: workers: expected an integer from 0 to 255, got 300
  return capture.length
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError | WriterError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let written = run check() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return if written > 0 { 0 } else { 1 }
}
```

<a id="SchemaReport.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(errors: &SchemaErrors, input: &[u8], source: string, options: ReportOptions) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes every problem in `errors`, read from `input`, to the ambient `Writer`. `source` names
the input, such as a file name, in each location.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
